mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the same month signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < previous month - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% from the previous month, sustained for two consecutive months, signals contraction in manufacturing output and reduced corporate earnings potential, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month - 1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 300,000 alongside a concurrent decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as markets anticipate higher corporate pricing power.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) of more than 5% from the previous month, sustained for two consecutive months, indicates households are saving more and spending less, which reduces aggregate demand and corporate revenues, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > previous month + 5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) of more than 0.5% month-over-month signals deflationary pressures, which can prompt central bank action and reduce corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline of more than 2% in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based contraction in economic activity, which reduces earnings and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month - 2% AND HOUST < previous month - 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
